prs.author: rxits
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves JSON-response-mode POST requests unresolved: handleRequest()'s Promise<Response> is only settled by send(), and cleanup deletes the stream mapping without resolving it, so the HTTP request hangs until the socket/platform timeout fires when close() runs mid-request. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves JSON-response-mode POST requests unresolved: handleRequest()'s Promise<Response> is only settled by send(), and cleanup deletes the stream mapping without resolving it, so the HTTP request hangs until the socket/platform timeout fires when close() runs mid-request. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs settle the same stuck JSON-mode response promise on close(), touching the same close()/cleanup code path in streamableHttp.ts and will conflict if merged separately. #2600 fixes a superset of the issue: in addition to settling pending JSON-mode POSTs, it also clears _requestToStreamMapping (previously left intact after close(), which let a send() suspended inside eventStore.storeEvent() resolve against a retired correlation and leak the response for the process lifetime), and its changeset explicitly notes the fix also applies to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692 covers only the JSON-mode hang, but does so with a more precise response: a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error rather than #2600's plain 404 'Session not found' status, and it groups outstanding request ids by stream to avoid overwriting an id that already has a real computed response (relevant for batched POSTs sharing one stream). Whichever PR is kept should incorporate #2692's -32000 JSON-RPC error formatting and batched-id grouping, since #2600's description doesn't mention that handling.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs settle the same stuck JSON-mode response promise on close(), touching the same close()/cleanup code path in streamableHttp.ts and will conflict if merged separately. #2600 fixes a superset of the issue: in addition to settling pending JSON-mode POSTs, it also clears _requestToStreamMapping (previously left intact after close(), which let a send() suspended inside eventStore.storeEvent() resolve against a retired correlation and leak the response for the process lifetime), and its changeset explicitly notes the fix also applies to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692 covers only the JSON-mode hang, but does so with a more precise response: a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error rather than #2600's plain 404 'Session not found' status, and it groups outstanding request ids by stream to avoid overwriting an id that already has a real computed response (relevant for batched POSTs sharing one stream). Whichever PR is kept should incorporate #2692's -32000 JSON-RPC error formatting and batched-id grouping, since #2600's description doesn't mention that handling.

members.title: fix(client/sse): release reader lock on disconnect to prevent ~50MB leak
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the identical bug: the StreamableHTTPClientTransport client never calls reader.releaseLock() on the SSE stream's ReadableStreamDefaultReader after the read loop in src/client/streamableHttp.ts exits (normally or via error), pinning the reader's internal buffer (~50MB for long-lived connections) and preventing GC. Both diffs target the exact same hunk (@@ -328,40 ...@@) and apply the same fix shape: wrap the existing `while (true) { ... }` read loop in a try block and release the lock afterward. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs settle the same stuck JSON-mode response promise on close(), touching the same close()/cleanup code path in streamableHttp.ts and will conflict if merged separately. #2600 fixes a superset of the issue: in addition to settling pending JSON-mode POSTs, it also clears _requestToStreamMapping (previously left intact after close(), which let a send() suspended inside eventStore.storeEvent() resolve against a retired correlation and leak the response for the process lifetime), and its changeset explicitly notes the fix also applies to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692 covers only the JSON-mode hang, but does so with a more precise response: a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error rather than #2600's plain 404 'Session not found' status, and it groups outstanding request ids by stream to avoid overwriting an id that already has a real computed response (relevant for batched POSTs sharing one stream). Whichever PR is kept should incorporate #2692's -32000 JSON-RPC error formatting and batched-id grouping, since #2600's description doesn't mention that handling.
